name_reason: Compliant with the global naming convention: data_fd2_ prefix (game global), battle_ core-table domain, descriptor pathfind_battle_tile_map_ptr that reflects both purpose (battle tile map base) and datatype (_ptr = 32-bit pointer). No Ghidra address residue in the name (battle_tile_map is semantic, not a hex address). Ghidra symbol name byte-identical to src/globals.
purpose: Caller-supplied base pointer to the 4-byte-per-tile battle tile map, shared by the movement-range flood-fill and destination pathfinder; used as the base for all origin/neighbour tile address arithmetic.
logic_summary: Both pathfind orchestrators store the full 32-bit tile-map base here at entry (MOV [0x60064],EAX: fd2_init_movement_range_floodfill @ 0x4E068, fd2_pathfind_to_destination @ 0x4E1EE), immediately read map_width from [ptr+0] and map_height from [ptr+2], then later read the pointer back as the base for origin-tile address math (ADD EBX,dword ptr [0x60064] @ 0x4E0B4 / 0x4E23A). Verified against disassembly of fd2_init_movement_range_floodfill: write at 0x4E068, header reads at 0x4E06D/0x4E075, base read at 0x4E0B4.
datatype: uint32 (4-byte pointer; Ghidra type=pointer LEN=4; holds a byte* to the 4-byte-per-tile battle tile map)
element_semantics: Single scalar pointer value (not an array): the base address of the battle tile map. map_width = byte at [ptr+0], map_height = byte at [ptr+2]; each tile is 4 bytes with the movement-range/path marker at tile offset +7-relative addressing computed by the orchestrators.
notes: Ghidra data plate at 0x60064 was null; created a concise PLATE_COMMENT reflecting the src conclusion (32-bit tile-map base, 2 writes + 2 reads by the two orchestrators, map_width/map_height from [ptr+0]/[ptr+2], non-const BSS runtime state) and saved the program. src comment block (pathfnd.c lines ~766-775) is already precise/accurate/ASCII and matches the disassembly byte-for-byte, so kept unchanged (no Edit to pathfnd.c). is_const=false: 2 game write-xrefs (0x4E068, 0x4E1EE).
